turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Describe a frontend feature you worked on. How did data move from a user action to the interface, and what did you implement?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Our dashboard was a great team effort. I helped arrange the filters and attended the React discussions. The senior engineer handled the data layer. I cannot describe the state or request sequence because I did not work on that part.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Walk me through a user-facing defect you investigated. What did you observe, and how did you decide what was causing it?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A customer mentioned old rows. I tried the page once and suggested it could be caching because that sounded familiar. I did not capture a trace or investigate which response was shown.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How did you check the change and decide it was ready for release?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I clicked Export and saw a file download. The team's pipeline was green. I did not inspect the file contents or know which assertions the suite contained.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What accessibility work or checks did you perform on this interface?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We used an established component library. I did not add accessibility behavior or perform accessibility checks myself; I assumed the library covered it.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Looking back, what were the limits of your ownership or evidence, and what would you investigate or ask for help with next?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I cannot separate our team's overall results from my own changes more precisely. I would ask the senior engineer about the data flow and review the tests before claiming the issue was fixed.
